message.content:
The first six primes are:

\[
2,3,5,7,11,13
\]

Among these, there is 1 even prime, \(2\), and 5 odd primes, \(3,5,7,11,13\).

The sum of two numbers is even if both numbers have the same parity:

- Both even
- Both odd

Since Paul and Jesse choose independently:

\[
P(\text{both even})=\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^2=\frac{1}{36}
\]

\[
P(\text{both odd})=\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^2=\frac{25}{36}
\]

So,

\[
P(\text{sum even})=\frac{1}{36}+\frac{25}{36}=\frac{26}{36}=\frac{13}{18}
\]

The answer is \(\frac{13}{18}\).
